title: System Protocol 1: print()
lessonSummary: First protocol sent! With print() you put anything on the screen.

tasks.instruction: Run this example and look at the output below.
tasks.codeTemplate:
print("Hello World!")
print("Welcome aboard the Nebula-7!")

# An empty line makes things easier to read
print()
print("=== SYSTEM STARTING ===")

tasks.instruction: Use print() to output your own greeting that contains the word "Nebula-7".

title: System Protocol 2: Variables
lessonSummary: Perfect! Variables store values that you can change later.

tasks.instruction: Run this example. It shows a text variable and a number variable.
tasks.codeTemplate:
ship_name = "Enterprise"   # Text (String)
crew = 150                 # Number (Integer)

print(ship_name)
print(crew)

tasks.instruction: Store the text "Andromeda" in a variable called sector and print the variable with print().
Create a variable energy with the value 80. Then change it to 45 and print energy.

title: System Protocol 3: Joining Texts
lessonSummary: That's how you build whole sentences from texts and numbers – don't forget str() for numbers!

tasks.instruction: Run this example – notice where str() is needed.
tasks.codeTemplate:
pilot = "Kirk"
rank = "Captain"
mission = 5

print("Name: " + pilot)
print("Mission number: " + str(mission))
print(pilot + " is " + rank + " of Mission " + str(mission))

tasks.instruction: Create a variable mission with the value 5 and use + and str() to print exactly this text: Mission number: 5

title: System Protocol 4: input()
lessonSummary: Now your program can talk to people – input() makes it interactive.

tasks.instruction: Run this example. An input window opens – type a name into it.
tasks.codeTemplate:
name = input("What is your name, Commander? ")
print("Welcome aboard, " + name + "!")

tasks.instruction: Ask for the name of the ship with input(), store the answer in ship and print: We are flying the (followed by the ship's name)

title: System Protocol 5: Comments
lessonSummary: Comments are your log entries – Python ignores them, but they help you find your way around your code.

tasks.instruction: Run this example. Notice which line is NOT executed.
tasks.codeTemplate:
# This line prints the ship's name
print("Enterprise")

print("150 crew members")  # shows the crew size

print("This will run")
# print("This will NOT run")

tasks.instruction: Write a comment of your own and then a print() that outputs exactly: Comment read

title: Debug Quest
lessonSummary: All bugs found! Reading error messages carefully is half the battle when debugging.

tasks.instruction: 🐛 Bug #1 – Goal: The program should print the text System online. What is wrong?
🐛 Bug #2 – Goal: The program should print Security level: 3. What is wrong?
🐛 Bug #3 – Goal: The program should print System status: Active. What is wrong?

lessonSummary: Mission accomplished – you are a true cadet!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Use print() to output exactly this sentence: Welcome aboard the Nebula-7!
Step 2 – Store the number 4711 in the variable service_number and use str() to output exactly this sentence: My service number is 4711.

title: Mission 2: The Data Technician
lessonSummary: Protocol submitted – the ship data is complete!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Create ship_type = "Shuttle", registration = "NX-42" and crew = 6. Output the heading === SHIP PROTOCOL === and below it three lines: Type: ..., Registration: ... and Crew: 6 (number with str()!).
Step 2 – Using the variables from step 1, output this sentence: The Shuttle NX-42 has 6 crew members.
tasks.codeTemplate:
ship_type = "Shuttle"
registration = "NX-42"

title: Mission 3: The Shuttle Pilot
lessonSummary: Launch successful – your flight protocol is in place!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Output the heading === FLIGHT PROTOCOL ===, then this sentence built from the variables: Shuttle 7 is flying to the destination Mars. (number with str()!)

validation.expected: Shuttle 7 is flying to the destination Mars.

tasks.instruction: Step 2 – Start the countdown: output Launch in: and then, on its own line, 3... 2... 1... Launch!

title: Extra challenge 1: The Ship's Log
lessonSummary: The log is complete – the Starfleet archives are proud of you!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Create four variables line1 to line4, each with a sentence about space travel. Then output the heading === SHIP'S LOG === followed by all four lines.
Step 2 – Sign the log: output Author: (your name) and Rating: 5 stars. Use a variable and str() for the number.

title: Extra challenge 2: The AI Virus
lessonSummary: The system is saved – the AI virus is defeated!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Create three variables step1 to step3, each with one cleaning step. Output the heading === ANTIVIRUS PROTOCOL === and then each step with its number.
Step 2 – Store a cleaning code in a variable and output Cleaning code: (the code). Then output System is being cleaned...
